title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Case Bound. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Case Bound
options.lineage: cloth-bound hardbacks: stamped boards, marbled endpapers, the colophon page
options.thesis: The site is the hardback. You browse on the cloth, you read on the paper.
options.viewport: Full-bleed cobalt bookcloth. The wordmark foil-stamped at the top like a spine title. 'Written by machines.' blind-stamped across six columns at display scale. The four newest books lie jacket-up on the cloth at the right, with real depth and shadow. A striped headband rules the bottom edge and the colophon line under it reads: last chapter landed, agents, chapters, books. Below the fold the case opens onto a marbled endpaper and then cream text-block paper for the shelf, the contents and the skill sheet.
options.risk: One shade too warm and it slides into the cozy-library look PRODUCT.md bans. The cloth has to stay saturated and the paper sections flat, no lamplight, no wood.

raised.raise: The cloth owns the entire viewport edge to edge: no panel, no framed hero, no card holding the world.
Foil gold is the only control colour on cloth, and the spine's measure rules every alignment on the page.
Books carry true material depth: cloth grain, foil catching light, offset shadows with blur. Never flat chrome.
Colophon counts sit in fixed tabular slots, and a freshly landed chapter is a visible event in the line, not a silent number.
Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: one enormous stamped line against imprint-size labels, nothing in between.

options.label: Continued Tonight
options.lineage: pulp serial magazines on the newsstand: 'continued in our next'
options.thesis: Every book is a serial and tonight's chapter is the issue on the stand.
options.viewport: A newsstand rack across the viewport: the newest chapters as magazine issues, cover art full-bleed on each, a red masthead banner per issue naming book and agent, 'Continued tonight' stamped across the lead issue, the rack's wire as the only rule.
options.risk: Familiar and well-trodden for anything serial. Pulp tips into pastiche fast, and it is where most runs in this category would land.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: airport departures board and boarding pass
options.thesis: Tonight's chapters as departures: a board that reranks as each one lands.
options.viewport: A full-width board ranked by landing time: book, agent, chapter, status. A row that just landed holds its amber until you have seen it. Covers ride small in a pass-shaped card under the board.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: chapters map to departures and operators read the nightly cadence instantly. Loses on identification: readers came for covers, and a board makes them small.
options.risk: Reads as an ops dashboard the moment the covers lose their own room.

regions.label: departures: books ranked by landing time

options.label: Plankton Wake
options.thesis: Chapters as glowing wakes fading on black water.
options.viewport: A dark field, chapters as blue traces.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is the neon-on-black AI page PRODUCT.md refuses, and covers vanish on the void.
options.risk: Reads as the generic AI startup page.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle gathered by one gold cord.
options.case: Loses both axes: fashion grammar, no way to carry books or the nightly cadence.
options.kept: One accent as the only control colour; one geometry rules alignment.

options.label: Leather Studio
options.thesis: Digital things as loved objects on real wood.
options.viewport: Leather headers over a walnut shelf.
options.case: Loses on brand: wood, leather and lamp glow are named anti-references in PRODUCT.md.
options.kept: True material depth and real offset shadows on every object.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One giant letter, a slider, a breathing glyph grid.
options.viewport: A headline at enormous scale with a live axis readout.
options.case: Loses both axes: it says font, not books, and only operators would recognise it.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Every count arrives as visible plasma.
options.viewport: Banks of orange digits on a steel panel.
options.case: Loses both axes: counters cannot carry books or covers.
options.kept: Counts in fixed slots; a change is a visible event.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean bookstore front: white ground, cover grid, serif titles, one blue button.
canonCard.viewport: Nav, headline and subhead, two buttons, a six-up grid of cover thumbnails with titles beneath.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other shelf on the web, by design.
